text:
marta: FYI onboarding cetus-65k-int3 for long-context smoke. Quick run shows clean until ~32k tokens then abrupt token corruption + kv fingerprint swap. Suspect RoPE wrap interacting with int3 interpolation.

marta: local repro command:
```bash
./dev_eval.sh --model cetus-65k-int3 --quant int3 --context 65536 --prompt tests/long_repeat_32k.txt --seed 42 --out /tmp/cetus32k.json
```

marta: key log excerpt (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15 09:02:11] i=32015 emit="and" p=0.14 kv_idx=32015 fp=0x7b1d
[2026-03-15 09:02:11] i=32767 emit="the" p=0.19 kv_idx=32767 fp=0x7bff
[2026-03-15 09:02:12] i=32768 emit="<CORRUPT>" p=0.94 kv_idx=32768 fp=0x8002  # phase flip and unexpected fingerprint
```

kai: does fp16 baseline hit same index? also try int4-hybrid if possible.

marta: fp16 baseline (cetus-65k-fp16) goes to 65k fine. int4-hybrid shows mild drift but not full corruption. int3 is the worst.

jules: can you dump kv keys around 32760-32770 and include phase field? Use tools/kv-dump --range 32760-32772 --hex.

marta: dump result:
```
32760 key=0xaaa1 len=256 phase=0x7ffd
32761 key=0xaab2 len=256 phase=0x7ffd
32767 key=0x7bff len=256 phase=0x7fff
32768 key=0x8002 len=256 phase=0x8002  # wrap here
32769 key=0x8003 len=256 phase=0x8003
```

rohan: that phase value jump lines up with a wrap at the 2^15 boundary. Two suspects: rotary exponent computation under quantized kernel or off-by-one in position->index mapping when context length surpasses model.max_pos or batching math. Did you enable the new rotary-scaling factor in the build?

marta: yes, rotary-scaling=on. toggling it off reduces corruption frequency but doesn't eliminate it.

jules: suggests quant math magnifies the discontinuity. Steps: 1) run short synthetic that forces wrap at low idx (e.g., repeat tokens until 512) to speed bisect; 2) build a float32 vs int3 trace of rotary exponent values for positions 32760..32770; 3) add kv fingerprint assert in regression suite.

tara: I can add a unit that mocks the exponent pipeline and compares fp32 vs quantized exponent at boundary. quick patch would catch drift in CI.

eval-bot: longctx-tail comparison (synthetic-holdout):
- cetus-65k-fp16 : ppl (0-32k)=7.9, (32k-65k)=8.0
- cetus-65k-int4 : ppl (0-32k)=8.1, (32k-65k)=8.6
- cetus-65k-int3 : ppl (0-32k)=8.4, (32k-65k)=11.4  <-- large tail regression (~+41% rel in tail)

marta: created bug #4291 and PR 1342 with short repro test (tests/regressions/phase_wrap_mini.py) that runs in CI and asserts kv fingerprint continuity. Added logs and kv-dump helper.

kai: good. assign to eng-ml/roto-quant and add to onboarding checklist: for any new int3/int4 profile, run phase_wrap_mini and longctx smoke. Also, add a telemetry metric to track sudden kv fingerprint deltas across requests.

jules: let's also run a commit bisect on quant kernels (last 5 commits touching kernels/rotary*). If bisect pins a commit, revert or patch quant interpolation.

rohan: note for triage: if bisect is noisy, use synthetic low-index reproducer and hardware-affine builds to isolate kernel vs build flags.

marta: will run bisect tomorrow and report back in this thread. Thanks all.
